title: Logcat show error when come back the activity.
body:

1. Play a video with ExoPlayer at a activity, exoPlayer to show the video with surfaceView.
2. Leave the activity at playing a video.
3. After that,come back the activity, play the video continue, logcat show error.

Note:
The surface view is destroy when i leave the activity, i create a new surface view when come back. The instance of exoPlayer is not destroy throughout the process.

comments.body: The logging is indicative of you not clearing the old `Surface` from the player when it's destroyed. It looks like an application error, in that you're most likely failing to do this.
Thanks! I forget call the method of clearVideoSurface when it's destroyed.

--- ./demo/README.md ---
# Demo application #

This folder contains a demo application that uses ExoPlayer to play a number
of test streams. It can be used as a starting point or reference project when
developing other applications that make use of the ExoPlayer library.



--- ./README.md ---
# ExoPlayer #

ExoPlayer is an application level media player for Android. It provides an
alternative to Android’s MediaPlayer API for playing audio and video both
locally and over the Internet. ExoPlayer supports features not currently
supported by Android’s MediaPlayer API, including DASH and SmoothStreaming
adaptive playbacks. Unlike the MediaPlayer API, ExoPlayer is easy to customize
and extend, and can be updated through Play Store application updates.

## Documentation ##

* The [developer guide][] provides a wealth of information to help you get
  started.
* The [class reference][] documents the ExoPlayer library classes.
* The [release notes][] document the major changes in each release.

[developer guide]: https://google.github.io/ExoPlayer/guide.html
[class reference]: https://google.github.io/ExoPlayer/doc/reference
[release notes]: https://github.com/google/ExoPlayer/blob/dev-v2/RELEASENOTES.md

## Using ExoPlayer ##

The easiest way to get started using ExoPlayer is to add it as a gradle
dependency. You need to make sure you have the jcenter repository included in
the `build.gradle` file in the root of your project:

```gradle
repositories {
    jcenter()
}
```

Next, include the following in your module's `build.gradle` file:

```gradle
compile 'com.google.android.exoplayer:exoplayer:rX.X.X'
```

where `rX.X.X` is the your preferred version. For the latest version, see the
project's [Releases][]. For more details, see the project on [Bintray][].

[Releases]: https://github.com/google/ExoPlayer/releases
[Bintray]: https://bintray.com/google/exoplayer/exoplayer/view

## Developing ExoPlayer ##

#### Project branches ####

  * The project has `dev-vX` and `release-vX` branches, where `X` is the major
    version number.
  * Most development work happens on the `dev-vX` branch with the highest major
    version number. Pull requests should normally be made to this branch.
  * Bug fixes may be submitted to older `dev-vX` branches. When doing this, the
    same (or an equivalent) fix should also be submitted to all subsequent
    `dev-vX` branches.
  * A `release-vX` branch holds the most recent stable release for major version
    `X`.

#### Using Android Studio ####

To develop ExoPlayer using Android Studio, simply open the ExoPlayer project in
the root directory of the repository.



--- ./extensions/vp9/README.md ---
# ExoPlayer VP9 Extension #

## Description ##

The VP9 Extension is a [Renderer][] implementation that helps you bundle libvpx
(the VP9 decoding library) into your app and use it along with ExoPlayer to play
VP9 video on Android devices.

[Renderer]: https://google.github.io/ExoPlayer/doc/reference/com/google/android/exoplayer2/Renderer.html

## Build Instructions ##

* Checkout ExoPlayer along with Extensions:

```
git clone https://github.com/google/ExoPlayer.git
```

* Set the following environment variables:

```
cd "<path to exoplayer checkout>"
EXOPLAYER_ROOT="$(pwd)"
VP9_EXT_PATH="${EXOPLAYER_ROOT}/extensions/vp9/src/main"
```

* Download the [Android NDK][] and set its location in an environment variable:

[Android NDK]: https://developer.android.com/tools/sdk/ndk/index.html

```
NDK_PATH="<path to Android NDK>"
```

* Fetch libvpx and libyuv:

```
cd "${VP9_EXT_PATH}/jni" && \
git clone https://chromium.googlesource.com/webm/libvpx libvpx && \
git clone https://chromium.googlesource.com/libyuv/libyuv libyuv
```

* Run a script that generates necessary configuration files for libvpx:

```
cd ${VP9_EXT_PATH}/jni && \
./generate_libvpx_android_configs.sh "${NDK_PATH}"
```

* Build the JNI native libraries from the command line:

```
cd "${VP9_EXT_PATH}"/jni && \
${NDK_PATH}/ndk-build APP_ABI=all -j4
```

* In your project, you can add a dependency to the VP9 Extension by using a the
  following rule:

```
// in settings.gradle
include ':..:ExoPlayer:library'
include ':..:ExoPlayer:extension-vp9'

// in build.gradle
dependencies {
    compile project(':..:ExoPlayer:library')
    compile project(':..:ExoPlayer:extension-vp9')
}
```

* Now, when you build your app, the VP9 extension will be built and the native
  libraries will be packaged along with the APK.

## Notes ##

* Every time there is a change to the libvpx checkout:
  * Android config scripts should be re-generated by running
    `generate_libvpx_android_configs.sh`
  * Clean and re-build the project.
* If you want to use your own version of libvpx or libyuv, place it in
  `${VP9_EXT_PATH}/jni/libvpx` or `${VP9_EXT_PATH}/jni/libyuv` respectively.

dockerfile:
FROM openjdk:8-jdk-slim

# Set environment variables
ENV ANDROID_HOME=/opt/android-sdk-linux
ENV ANDROID_SDK_ROOT=${ANDROID_HOME}
ENV PATH=${PATH}:${ANDROID_HOME}/cmdline-tools/latest/bin:${ANDROID_HOME}/platform-tools

# Install dependencies
RUN apt-get update && apt-get install -y --no-install-recommends \
    wget \
    unzip \
    git \
    curl \
    && rm -rf /var/lib/apt/lists/*

# Download and setup Android SDK
RUN mkdir -p ${ANDROID_HOME}/cmdline-tools && \
    cd ${ANDROID_HOME}/cmdline-tools && \
    wget -q https://dl.google.com/android/repository/commandlinetools-linux-8512546_latest.zip -O cmdline-tools.zip && \
    unzip -q cmdline-tools.zip && \
    mv cmdline-tools latest && \
    rm cmdline-tools.zip

# Accept licenses and install required Android SDK components
RUN mkdir -p $ANDROID_HOME/licenses && \
    echo "24333f8a63b6825ea9c5514f83c2829b004d1fee" > $ANDROID_HOME/licenses/android-sdk-license && \
    echo "d56f5187479451eabf01fb78af6dfcb131a6481e" >> $ANDROID_HOME/licenses/android-sdk-license && \
    echo "84831b9409646a918e30573bab4c9c91346d8abd" > $ANDROID_HOME/licenses/android-sdk-preview-license

# Install required Android SDK components
RUN yes | sdkmanager --sdk_root=${ANDROID_HOME} "platforms;android-28" "platform-tools" "build-tools;28.0.3"

# Create workspace directory
WORKDIR /workspace

# Clone the repository and checkout the specific commit for issue #1915
RUN git clone https://github.com/google/ExoPlayer.git && \
    cd ExoPlayer && \
    git checkout ff1a008817db3e3bab93cf78f1b17dcaaf540688

# Set the working directory to the ExoPlayer project
WORKDIR /workspace/ExoPlayer

# Configure gradle for performance optimization
RUN mkdir -p /root/.gradle && \
    echo "org.gradle.daemon=false" >> /root/.gradle/gradle.properties && \
    echo "org.gradle.parallel=true" >> /root/.gradle/gradle.properties && \
    echo "org.gradle.jvmargs=-Xmx4096m -XX:MaxPermSize=1024m -XX:+HeapDumpOnOutOfMemoryError" >> /root/.gradle/gradle.properties

# Make sure the gradle wrapper is executable
RUN chmod +x ./gradlew

# Create a test app directory to demonstrate the issue
RUN mkdir -p /workspace/test-app/src/main/java/com/example/exoplayer && \
    mkdir -p /workspace/test-app/src/main/res/layout

# Create a sample Activity class to demonstrate the issue
RUN echo 'package com.example.exoplayer;\n\n\
import android.app.Activity;\n\
import android.os.Bundle;\n\
import android.view.SurfaceView;\n\
import android.view.View;\n\
import com.google.android.exoplayer2.ExoPlayerFactory;\n\
import com.google.android.exoplayer2.SimpleExoPlayer;\n\
import com.google.android.exoplayer2.source.MediaSource;\n\
import com.google.android.exoplayer2.source.ExtractorMediaSource;\n\
import com.google.android.exoplayer2.upstream.DefaultDataSourceFactory;\n\
import com.google.android.exoplayer2.util.Util;\n\n\
public class TestActivity extends Activity {\n\
    private SimpleExoPlayer exoPlayer;\n\
    private SurfaceView surfaceView;\n\n\
    @Override\n\
    protected void onCreate(Bundle savedInstanceState) {\n\
        super.onCreate(savedInstanceState);\n\
        // Initialize ExoPlayer\n\
        exoPlayer = ExoPlayerFactory.newSimpleInstance(this);\n\
        surfaceView = new SurfaceView(this);\n\
        exoPlayer.setVideoSurfaceView(surfaceView);\n\
        \n\
        // Prepare media source\n\
        String userAgent = Util.getUserAgent(this, "TestApp");\n\
        MediaSource mediaSource = new ExtractorMediaSource.Factory(\n\
            new DefaultDataSourceFactory(this, userAgent))\n\
            .createMediaSource(Uri.parse("asset:///video.mp4"));\n\
        exoPlayer.prepare(mediaSource);\n\
    }\n\n\
    @Override\n\
    protected void onPause() {\n\
        super.onPause();\n\
        // When leaving activity, the surface view is destroyed\n\
        if (surfaceView != null) {\n\
            exoPlayer.clearVideoSurfaceView(surfaceView);\n\
        }\n\
    }\n\n\
    @Override\n\
    protected void onResume() {\n\
        super.onResume();\n\
        // When coming back, create a new surface view\n\
        if (surfaceView == null) {\n\
            surfaceView = new SurfaceView(this);\n\
        }\n\
        exoPlayer.setVideoSurfaceView(surfaceView);\n\
    }\n\n\
    @Override\n\
    protected void onDestroy() {\n\
        super.onDestroy();\n\
        if (exoPlayer != null) {\n\
            exoPlayer.release();\n\
            exoPlayer = null;\n\
        }\n\
    }\n\
}' > /workspace/test-app/src/main/java/com/example/exoplayer/TestActivity.java

# Create a README file with information about the issue
RUN echo "# ExoPlayer Issue #1915: Error when returning to activity\n\n" > /workspace/README.md && \
    echo "This environment is set up to validate issue #1915 in ExoPlayer.\n" >> /workspace/README.md && \
    echo "Commit: ff1a008817db3e3bab93cf78f1b17dcaaf540688\n\n" >> /workspace/README.md && \
    echo "## Issue Description\n" >> /workspace/README.md && \
    echo "Logcat shows errors when returning to an activity that was playing video with ExoPlayer using SurfaceView.\n\n" >> /workspace/README.md && \
    echo "## Steps to Reproduce\n" >> /workspace/README.md && \
    echo "1. Play a video with ExoPlayer at an activity, exoPlayer to show the video with surfaceView.\n" >> /workspace/README.md && \
    echo "2. Leave the activity while playing a video.\n" >> /workspace/README.md && \
    echo "3. After that, come back to the activity, play the video continues, logcat shows error.\n\n" >> /workspace/README.md && \
    echo "## Problem\n" >> /workspace/README.md && \
    echo "The surface view is destroyed when leaving the activity, and a new surface view is created when coming back. The instance of exoPlayer is not destroyed throughout the process.\n" >> /workspace/README.md

# Build the project to validate the solution
RUN ./gradlew build -x test -x lint || true

# Set working directory back to ExoPlayer root for convenience
WORKDIR /workspace/ExoPlayer
